title: The Anatomy of a Magical Web Page

learningObjectives.description: Explain how a website groups related web pages.
Explain that HTML describes content meaning and page structure.
Identify HTML elements, opening tags and closing tags.
Use a main heading and a paragraph appropriately.
Recognize the structure of body fragments and a basic HTML document.
Find and repair simple mismatched-tag or structure mistakes.

variants.intro: Build a tiny spellbook page with real HTML. Recognize each part, write a heading and paragraph, then repair a mismatched tag.

sections.title: Websites, pages and HTML
paragraphs: A web page is a document a browser can display. A website groups related pages, usually connected by links.
HTML means HyperText Markup Language. It describes the meaning and structure of content; CSS styles it, and JavaScript can add behavior. This lesson uses HTML only.

paragraphs:
In

,

is a closing tag. The tags and content together form an element.
Use h1 for a main heading and p for a paragraph. HTML has h1 through h6 for heading levels; choose them for structure rather than just size.

sections.title: Structure and repair
paragraphs: A full document has an html root, a head for information such as the browser-tab title, and a body for the page content. Our small practice fragments contain just body content.
Browsers can recover from some HTML mistakes, so looking okay does not prove the source is right. Read the tag names, match each pair, and check the page’s order.

variants.intro: Create a small, meaningful web page. Learn the difference between document metadata and visible content, practice headings and paragraphs, then write your own complete introductory document.

sections.title: A document on the web
paragraphs: A website is a collection of related web pages. A web page is a document viewed in a browser; a browser tab displays a particular page.

HTML (HyperText Markup Language) marks up content and structure. It is not a general programming language: HTML alone does not describe arbitrary computational logic. CSS and JavaScript have different roles.

sections.title: Elements communicate meaning
paragraphs:
An opening tag, content and closing tag form an element, such as

Welcome.

. A main heading uses h1; a paragraph uses p.
Headings h1–h6 represent levels of structure. For this introductory single-section page, use one main heading followed by a paragraph; do not choose heading levels only for their visual size.

sections.title: The document skeleton
paragraphs: <!doctype html> declares modern HTML. The html element is the root; lang="en" identifies English. The head holds metadata: charset="utf-8" declares encoding, and title supplies the browser-tab title.

The body contains visible content. Our independent exercise requires an explicit head/body skeleton, one h1 and one p. Repair mismatched tags even if a browser would recover; our strict lesson checker is not a full HTML validator.

choices.text: HTML and a website are the same thing.
choices.feedback: Separate the collection of pages from the language describing a document.

choices.text: A website groups related pages; HTML describes a page’s structure.
choices.feedback: The website is the collection; HTML is a markup language used for documents.

questions.prompt: Where do browser-tab title and visible main heading belong?

choices.text: Both must go in head.
choices.feedback: A visible heading belongs in body, while title is document metadata.

choices.text: title in head; h1 in body.
choices.feedback: The head describes the document; body contains its visible content.

questions.prompt: A browser displays mismatched tags without an obvious problem. What follows?

choices.text: Assume the source is correct because it displays.
choices.feedback: A forgiving display does not establish correct source structure.

choices.text: Review and correct the source; browser recovery can hide mistakes.
choices.feedback: Browsers repair some errors; explicit matching tags keep the intended structure clear.

variants.audienceLabel: AI learning pathway · deterministic HTML data
variants.intro: Inspect explicit structure constraints and finite assessment cases, then try the local workbench. Submitted source stays data; no browser markup or agent code is executed.

sections.title: Document and language identities
paragraphs: A website groups related web pages. HTML is a markup language for document semantics and structure. It is distinct from CSS styling and JavaScript behavior.
The lesson accepts a deliberately bounded attribute-free h1/p fragment or an explicit restricted document skeleton, not general HTML.

sections.title: Element and structure constraints
paragraphs:
An element such as

Text

contains opening/closing tags and text. Task shapes require either a single h1, an h1 followed by p, or a full declared document skeleton.
In a document, metadata such as title belongs in head; the main heading and paragraph belong in body. This checker requires explicit end tags even where HTML itself may allow omission.

sections.title: Deterministic repair and safe display
paragraphs: Correct tag-pair and order mistakes, then reassess against the same task constraints. Matching the restricted grammar is task performance, not general validation or retained AI learning.
A successful result produces a small text model. Fixed React components display its text; the submitted HTML is never used as DOM markup, an iframe document or tool instructions.

choices.text: An agent execution permission format.
choices.feedback: Document source is data, not execution authorization.

choices.text: A markup language for document meaning and structure.
choices.feedback: HTML describes documents; this lesson grants no tool permissions.

questions.prompt: What makes the supplied p example a complete element?

choices.text: Only its final character.
choices.feedback: Inspect the opening marker, content and closing marker together.

choices.text: Its opening tag, text content and matching closing tag.
choices.feedback: The paired markers and content form the element.

questions.prompt: Where must the visible heading be in the document task?

choices.text: Inside title as raw nested markup.
choices.feedback: title is plain-text metadata in the head, not a container for visible body structure.

choices.text: Inside body, following the declared head.
choices.feedback: The body contains visible page content.

practiceTasks.title: Construct a restricted document
practiceTasks.instruction: Submit the full English document skeleton with your own nonempty title, h1 and p. All content must be plain text within the documented limits.
